tasks.title: Add logout button to authenticated calculator view
tasks.description:
1. WHAT: Add a logout button that sets `isAuthenticated` back to `false`, returning the user to the login screen.
2. READ FIRST: Read `src/App.tsx` (lines 15-60 — auth state and both render branches), `src/App.css` (for existing styles and theme variables), `src/App.test.tsx` (for existing test patterns and the `renderAndLogin` helper).
3. FILES: Modify `src/App.tsx` — add a `handleLogout` function that calls `setIsAuthenticated(false)` and render a logout button in the authenticated view (the second return block, around line 52-58). Add a `<button>` with class `logout-button` and text `Logout` near the top of the authenticated layout (e.g., next to the h1). Modify `src/App.css` — add `.logout-button` styles that use the existing theme CSS variables (`--app-text`, `--button-bg-start`, `--button-border`, etc.) for both light and dark themes. Style it as a small, unobtrusive button positioned near the header. Modify `src/App.test.tsx` — add tests: (a) after login, a 'Logout' button is visible, (b) clicking the Logout button returns to the login screen (login form is visible again, calculator title is not).
4. APPROACH: Add `handleLogout` as a simple state setter `() => setIsAuthenticated(false)`. Place the logout button inside the authenticated `.app` div, above or beside the `<h1>`. Use existing CSS variables for theming consistency.
5. PATTERNS: Follow the same test patterns in `src/App.test.tsx` — use the existing `renderAndLogin()` helper, then interact with the logout button via `screen.getByRole('button', { name: /logout/i })`.
acceptance_criteria: After logging in, a 'Logout' button is visible on the calculator page
Clicking the 'Logout' button returns the user to the login screen
The logout button is styled consistently in both light and dark themes

Also run TypeScript type-check to catch any type errors.
